toegepas.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
toegepas.voor: het nie in die rivier begin nie
toegepas.na: kom nie uit die rivier self nie
toegepas.rede_vinder: An object 'beginning' in a river is unidiomatic; 'kom nie uit die rivier self nie' says the same thing naturally.
toegepas.fout: 'het nie in die rivier begin nie' copies English 'didn't start in the river'; an object does not 'begin' somewhere in Afrikaans.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal says the same thing, that the bag did not originate in the river, in natural Afrikaans, and it does not change the next sentence.

toegepas.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
toegepas.voor: Hierdie les kyk na drie soorte besoedeling in water.
toegepas.na: In hierdie les kyk ons na drie soorte besoedeling in water.
toegepas.rede_vinder: A lesson that 'looks at' something is a calque of English; Afrikaans prefers 'In hierdie les kyk ons na'.
toegepas.fout: 'Hierdie les kyk na' is a calque of English 'This lesson looks at'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'In hierdie les kyk ons na' is the natural Afrikaans form and the content is unchanged.

toegepas.voor: Kieme is nie 'n stof wat oplos
toegepas.na: Kieme is nie stowwe wat oplos
toegepas.rede_vinder: The plural subject 'Kieme' should be matched by the plural 'stowwe', as it is by 'dinge' later in the sentence.
toegepas.fout: The singular 'n stof' clashes with the plural subject 'Kieme' and the plural 'dinge' later in the same sentence.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The plural 'stowwe' fixes the number mismatch and echoes the lesson's 'onoplosbare stowwe' and 'oplosbare stowwe' without moving the meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Bevat' is the natural verb for what a substance has in it; 'dra' suggests carrying.
toegepas.fout: 'kieme dra' is a loose verb for what waste has in it.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'bevat' is the exact Afrikaans verb for what a substance has in it, and no qualifier or protected wording is touched.

toegepas.voor: skoon lyk en tog kieme dra
toegepas.na: skoon lyk en tog kieme bevat
toegepas.rede_vinder: Water 'bevat' germs; 'dra' is unnatural here and repeats the previous verb.
toegepas.fout: 'tog kieme dra' is an unnatural verb for water that has germs in it.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'tog kieme bevat' is natural and exact, matches change 4, and leaves the protected 'waarin sulke kieme is' intact.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: los in die water op en versprei deur die water
laat_vaar_vorige.na: los in die water op en versprei daardeur
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Avoids repeating 'die water' twice in one short clause.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The repetition is mild and plain for Grade 6, while 'daardeur' is stiffer and can be read as 'as a result of that', which risks moving the meaning.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: wat te klein is om te sien en mense siek kan maak
laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat mense siek kan maak en te klein is om te sien
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The original can be misread as 'too small to see and to make people sick'; reordering removes the ambiguity without changing the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The finite 'kan maak' already ties the second clause to 'wat', so the misreading is unlikely, and the original order keeps visibility first in line with the other two list items.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Subject-first order reads more naturally here and is easier for a Grade 6 learner; the protected wording that follows is untouched.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Fronting 'So 'n siekte' deliberately links back to the previous sentence; the proposal is a lateral reorder that loosens that link.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: siek kan maak of kan doodmaak
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The repeated 'kan' is redundant; 'siek of dood kan maak' is shorter and more natural with the same meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: This is a glossary definition and the repeated 'kan' is correct Afrikaans, so there is no real fault to justify rewording it.
